Setup your Better Thermostat to integrate with Home Assistant

**Detailed information:** {docs_url}

data.name: Name
data.off_temperature: The outdoor temperature when the thermostat should turn off
data.tolerance: Tolerance, to prevent the thermostat from turning on and off too often
data.window_off_delay: Delay before the thermostat should turn off when the window is opened
data.window_off_delay_after: Delay before the thermostat should turn on when the window is closed
data.door_off_delay: Delay before the thermostat should turn off when the door is opened
data.door_off_delay_after: Delay before the thermostat should turn on when the door is closed
data.weather: Weather entity to get the outdoor temperature

data_description.name: The name of this thermostat and its device in Home Assistant.
data_description.thermostat: The radiator thermostats (TRVs) of this room. Better Thermostat drives all of them together.
data_description.cooler: Optional. An air conditioner or another climate entity that cools this room alongside the thermostats.
data_description.temperature_sensor: The room temperature sensor Better Thermostat controls by. Place it away from the radiator.
data_description.humidity_sensor: Optional. Its reading is shown on the thermostat and used by the humidity device triggers.
data_description.window_sensors: Optional. A sensor or group that reports an open window; while it does, the heating pauses.
data_description.door_sensors: Optional. Works like the window sensor, with delays of its own.
data_description.off_temperature: Heating turns off once the outdoor temperature reaches this value and back on once it is 1 °C (1.8 °F) below it. The current outdoor temperature is averaged over about a day.
data_description.tolerance: How far the room may cool below the target before heating starts again: a target of 20 and a tolerance of 0.3 heat again at 19.7.
data_description.window_off_delay: How long a window has to stay open before the heating pauses.
data_description.window_off_delay_after: How long every window has to stay closed before the heating resumes.
data_description.door_off_delay: How long a door has to stay open before the heating pauses.
data_description.door_off_delay_after: How long every door has to stay closed before the heating resumes.
data_description.outdoor_sensor: Optional. Supplies the outdoor temperature for the outdoor threshold and takes precedence over the weather entity.
data_description.weather: Optional. Supplies the outdoor temperature when no outdoor sensor is selected.
data_description.target_temp_min: The lowest target you can set. Auto takes the range your devices report.
data_description.target_temp_max: The highest target you can set. Auto takes the range your devices report.
data_description.target_temp_step: How far the target moves per step. Auto takes the coarsest step your thermostats report.
data_description.presets: Select the presets you want to be available for this thermostat.

data.heat_auto_swapped: If 'auto' means 'heat' for your TRV and you want to swap it
data.child_lock: Ignore all inputs on the TRV like a child lock
data.homematicip: If you use HomematicIP, you should enable this to slow down the requests to prevent the duty cycle
data.valve_maintenance: If your thermostat has no own maintenance mode, you can use this one
data.no_off_system_mode: Use the minimum temperature instead of 'off'

data_description.protect_overheating: Some TRVs don't close the valve completely when the temperature is reached. Or the radiator has a lot of rest heat. This can cause overheating. This option can prevent this.
data_description.heat_auto_swapped: For a TRV whose heating mode is called 'auto': Better Thermostat then sends 'auto' to heat.
data_description.child_lock: Locks the buttons of the TRV where it has a child lock, so changes made on the TRV itself are ignored.
data_description.homematicip: Sends commands less often so HomematicIP devices stay within their duty cycle.
data_description.valve_maintenance: Opens and closes the valve now and then so it does not get stuck. For TRVs without a maintenance routine of their own.
data_description.calibration:
How the calibration is applied on the TRV
***Target Temperature Based***: Apply the calibration to the target temperature.
***Offset Based***: Apply the calibration to the temperature offset.
data_description.calibration_mode:
How the calibration is calculated
***(AI) Time Based (Default)***: Learns the heating power of your room over time and derives the calibration from it.
***External Sensor Offset Only***: Corrects the TRV's internal sensor with your external temperature sensor. No controller runs on top.
***MPC Predictive (Beta)***: Predicts the room temperature and calculates a valve opening from it. Learns your room's thermal behaviour.
***(AI) MPC v2 (QP + Kalman, experimental)***: Estimates the room state with a Kalman filter and calculates a valve opening with a model predictive controller. The MPC v2 room size setting picks the room model: learned from the room (Auto) or fixed for a room size (Small, Medium, Large).
***Aggressive***: Adds a boost to the calibration while the room is heating and skips the tolerance delay, so the TRV starts heating sooner. Useful if your room heats slowly.
***TPI Controller***: Calculates heating duty cycles from the temperature difference.
***PID Controller***: Calculates a valve opening from the temperature error with a proportional, integral and derivative term.
***No Calibration***: Sends the target temperature to the TRV unchanged and applies no correction.
data_description.no_off_system_mode: With this option, Better Thermostat sends the TRV its minimum temperature in place of 'off'. A TRV that reports its minimum temperature counts as switched off: once every TRV of the room is off and no window or door is open, the room switches off, and turning a knob up switches it back on. A TRV that offers no 'off' mode receives its minimum temperature without this option. Enable it for a TRV whose 'off' mode does not work, or for a TRV without an 'off' mode whose knob should switch Better Thermostat on and off.
data_description.mpc_v2_plant_preset:
Only used by the MPC v2 calibration mode.
***Auto***: Derives the room model from what Better Thermostat has learned about the room, such as its heat-loss rate.
***Small, Medium or Large room***: Starts from a fixed room model for that room size.

confirm.title: The related entity {entity} is missing
confirm.description:
The reason for this is that the entity ({entity}) is not available in your Home Assistant.

You can fix this by checking if the battery of the device is full or reconnecting it to HA. Make sure that the entity is back in HA before you continue.

If the entity was renamed or the device was replaced, its entity ID changed and Better Thermostat still looks for {entity}. Open the settings of this Better Thermostat (Settings → Devices & services → Better Thermostat → Configure) and select the new entity. This issue clears itself once the entity is available again or no Better Thermostat uses it any more.

degraded_mode.title: BT: {name} - sensor error: {sensors} running in degraded mode
degraded_mode.description:
Better Thermostat is running in degraded mode because some sensors are unavailable: {sensors}

The thermostat keeps controlling and steps down gracefully:
- If the room temperature sensor is unavailable, the average of the TRV-internal temperatures substitutes for it.
- If neither the room sensor nor any TRV temperature is usable, the thermostat stops adjusting and keeps the last commanded state; frost protection stays active.
- If a contact sensor (window or door) is unavailable, the contact is assumed closed and heating continues; a lost sensor must not stop heating.
- If outdoor/weather sensors are unavailable, heating stays enabled.

Check whether the affected devices have battery or connectivity problems. This issue clears itself once all sensors are available again.

invalid_window_state.title: BT: {name} - invalid window sensor state
invalid_window_state.description:
The window sensor for Better Thermostat {name} reported an unrecognized state: {state}.

Expected states are: 'on', 'off', 'true', 'false', 'open', 'closed'.

Please check your window sensor configuration.

invalid_door_state.title: BT: {name} - invalid door sensor state
invalid_door_state.description:
The door sensor for Better Thermostat {name} reported an unrecognized state: {state}.

Expected states are: 'on', 'off', 'true', 'false', 'open', 'closed'.

Please check your door sensor configuration.

invalid_external_temperature.title: BT: {name} - invalid external temperature
invalid_external_temperature.description:
The external temperature sensor for Better Thermostat {name} reported an implausible value: {value}.

The reading was outside the plausible range and has been ignored. Please check your temperature sensor configuration.

shared_trv.title: BT: {trv} is controlled by more than one Better Thermostat
shared_trv.description: The thermostat {trv} belongs to these Better Thermostats: {entries}. They write competing target temperatures and modes to it. Remove it from all but one of them in their settings; this issue clears itself afterwards.

run_valve_maintenance.name: Run valve maintenance now
run_valve_maintenance.description: Run the valve maintenance cycle immediately for this Better Thermostat entity.

reset_heating_power.name: Reset heating power
reset_heating_power.description: Reset the heating power to its default value.

reset_pid_learnings.name: Reset PID learnings
reset_pid_learnings.description: Clear all learned PID state for this entity.

apply_pid_defaults.name: Apply PID defaults after reset
apply_pid_defaults.description: If enabled, seeds the current target bucket(s) with PID default gains (kp/ki/kd). You can override defaults below.

defaults_kp.name: Default kp
defaults_kp.description: Proportional gain to seed after reset (falls back to BalanceParams.kp if not provided).

defaults_ki.name: Default ki
defaults_ki.description: Integral gain to seed after reset (falls back to BalanceParams.ki if not provided).

defaults_kd.name: Default kd
defaults_kd.description: Derivative gain to seed after reset (falls back to BalanceParams.kd if not provided).

state.window_open: turned off because a window was opened
state.window_close: resumed heating because a window was closed
state.summer_mode_on: turned off because the outdoor temperature is too high
state.summer_mode_off: resumed heating because the outdoor temperature dropped
state.weather_forecast_missing: resumed heating because the weather forecast is unavailable
state.degraded_mode_entered: entered degraded mode because some sensors are unavailable
state.degraded_mode_resolved: exited degraded mode because all sensors are available
state.door_open: turned off because a door was opened
state.door_close: resumed heating because a door was closed
